content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "Using 10-K segment and MD&A disclosures, count the number of major customers/suppliers each firm reports as accounting for >10% of revenues or purchases. Build a Herfindahl-style concentration index from the disclosed percentages. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June; the measure is the customer-revenue Herfindahl.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk and bargaining-power disadvantages, requiring a risk premium that is slow to be priced by investors who ignore relationship disclosures.", "higher_returns_for": "high concentration (few dominant customers)"}, {"name": "Accrual Volatility", "construction": "Compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by average total assets) each year for the prior 5 fiscal years, then take the standard deviation of these annual accruals. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "High variability in accruals signals low earnings quality and greater information risk about true cash-generating ability, commanding higher expected returns as compensation.", "higher_returns_for": "high accrual volatility"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Growth", "construction": "For firms reporting order backlog in the 10-K (common in manufacturing/aerospace/tech), compute year-over-year growth in reported backlog scaled by total assets or sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Growing backlog is a forward-looking demand signal not captured in current earnings; markets underreact to this soft-order information, so high backlog growth predicts positive future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high backlog growth"}, {"name": "R&D Acceleration", "construction": "Compute R&D expense scaled by sales for the current year minus the average R&D-to-sales over the prior three years. This captures the second-order change (acceleration) in innovation intensity. Rank cross-sectionally each June among R&D-reporting firms.", "rationale": "Firms accelerating R&D investment signal expanding growth opportunities that are conservatively expensed and undervalued, leading to positive drift as innovation outputs materialize.", "higher_returns_for": "high R&D acceleration"}, {"name": "Dividend-Repurchase Mix Shift", "construction": "Measure total share repurchases (from cash flow statement, purchase of common stock) as a fraction of total payout (dividends plus repurchases) over the trailing year, and compute the change versus the prior year. Rank firms cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "A shift toward repurchases over dividends reflects management's belief that shares are undervalued and offers flexibility; markets underprice this signaling content.", "higher_returns_for": "high increase in repurchase share of payout"}, {"name": "Inventory-Sales Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories minus year-over-year growth in sales, scaled to a comparable basis. A positive value indicates inventory building faster than demand. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Inventory outpacing sales foreshadows future markdowns, write-offs, and weakening demand that investors are slow to recognize; low divergence firms outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low inventory-sales divergence (sales growing faster than inventory)"}, {"name": "Tax-Book Income Gap", "construction": "Estimate taxable income by grossing up current tax expense by the statutory rate, then compute the ratio of estimated taxable income to pre-tax book income. Rank firms cross-sectionally; the measure flags large book-over-tax positive gaps.", "rationale": "Large positive book-tax gaps indicate aggressive earnings management inflating reported book income relative to conservative tax income, predicting lower future returns as gaps reverse.", "higher_returns_for": "low book-tax gap (taxable income high relative to book income)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Smoothness", "construction": "Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capital expenditures (capex/total assets) over the prior 5 fiscal years. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Lumpy, erratic investment reflects poor planning and greater real-option uncertainty; smooth, predictable investors are lower-risk and command lower returns, so the risk premium accrues to erratic-capex firms.", "higher_returns_for": "high capex volatility (erratic investment)"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Change per Size", "construction": "Compute the change in the number of I/B/E/S analysts covering the firm over the trailing 12 months, orthogonalized to (divided by) log market capitalization. Rank cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "An increase in analyst coverage beyond what size predicts reflects rising institutional attention and reduced information asymmetry, generating positive returns as the investor base broadens.", "higher_returns_for": "high size-adjusted increase in coverage"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Stability Score", "construction": "Compute quarterly gross margin (gross profit/sales) over the prior 12 quarters and calculate the standard deviation. Combine with the level of gross margin into a z-score composite favoring high-and-stable margins. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Firms with high, stable gross margins possess durable competitive advantages and pricing power that the market underappreciates relative to headline earnings, producing sustained outperformance.", "higher_returns_for": "high and stable gross margins"}]}
